Mr. G. N. Rout, Advocate
 Coram:
 Mr. Justice D.Dash
Mr. Justice G. Satapathy Order Order No. 11.01.2024
01. 1.
This matter is taken up through hybrid arrangement (virtual/physical) mode.

2. The Petitioners, by filing this writ petition, have invoked the jurisdiction of this Court under Article 226 & 227 of the Constitution of India, with a prayer to direct the Opposite Party to dispose of the application filed by the Petitioners under section 28-A of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short, 'the L.A. Act').
3.

Learned Counsel for the Petitioners submits that award being passed in two Proceedings under section 18 of the L.A. Act, which had been numbered as MJC NO.188 of 1997 and 195 of 1997 before the Referral Court arising out of L.A. Case // 2 // No.15 of 1994

, the Petitioners banking upon the provision contained in section 28-A of the L.A. Act has applied for being similarly treated and granted with the enhanced compensation since his land as described in the petition had also been acquired under the same notification.
He submits that in view of pendency of such application for quite a long time, the Petitioners are deprived of the benefits to which they are entitled in law.

4. Learned Additional Standing Counsel filing the copy of the written instruction which he has obtained pursuant to our order dated 06.12.2023, which is taken on record does not dispute the position that the land described in the petition under section 28-A of the L.A. filed by the Petitioners had been acquired under the same notification whereby the land concerned in the Referral Proceeding numbered as MJC No.195 of 1997 had been acquired and that the Referral Court has passed an award determining just and proper compensation.
He, however, is not in a position to submit about further challenge to said award if any.
